title: [ML] ensure that inference index primary shards are available before attempting to load model

timeline.message: [ML] fixing trained model loading so it waits for indices
timeline.author: Benjamin Trent

diff.patch:
@@ -63,6 +63,7 @@ public TransportCreateTrainedModelAllocationAction(
                 trainedModelAllocationService,
                 clusterService,
                 deploymentManager,
+                indexNameExpressionResolver,
                 transportService.getTaskManager(),
                 threadPool,
                 licenseState

timeline.body:
when we attempt to load trained models nodes, we should wait for the inference indices primary shards to be available before attempting to load the models. Otherwise attempting to load the models is a waste of time and could cause errors.

closes: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/85438

timeline.author: Benjamin Trent

timeline.body: Hi @benwtrent, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
This should not be required with the other changes.

reply.body: @davidkyle It ensures that the index is around before even bothering to wait around for the model. Correct, it doesn't do anything for the node assignment/allocation. But since the trigger trained model loading is in 5s intervals, I thought it good to not bother waiting for that until shards are available.

timeline.body:
```suggestion
                InferenceIndexConstants.INDEX_PATTERN, InferenceIndexConstants.nativeDefinitionStore(), 
```

`InferenceIndexConstants.INDEX_PATTERN` for the config and `InferenceIndexConstants.nativeDefinitionStore()` for the vocab and model definition.

Thanks for fixing this it is exactly the change I had in mind.

In theory the index the model definition is stored in is configurable if not in practice. In future we may have to add the storage index to `TrainedModelAllocationMetadata` then the node service can pick it up.

+If configured, a node can open a TCP port when the node is in a ready state. A node is deemed
+ready when it has successfully joined a cluster. In a single node configuration, the node is
+said to be ready, when it's able to accept requests.
+
+To enable the readiness TCP port, use the `readiness.port` setting. The port is
+always bound to the loopback address, which defaults to the IPv4 loopback address `127.0.0.1`.
+To bind the readiness port to the IPv6 loopback address `::1`,

+
+If the node leaves the cluster, or the <<put-shutdown,Shutdown API>> is used to mark the node
+for shutdown, the readiness port is immediately closed.
+
+A successful connection to the readiness TCP port signals that the {es} node is ready. When a client
+connects to the readiness port, the server simply terminates the socket connection. No data is sent back
+to the client. If a client cannot connect to the readiness port, the node is not ready.
